body:
@petebacondarwin and @gkalpak already started looking into this issue a few days ago, but it is still occurring. Pete, George, can you please post the most recent status update here?

@vicb - fyi since you are the caretaker that sees this one quite often.

AFAICT, there are currently 3 flakes that come up:

1. `expected 0 to be greater than 0`
    They occur in [these specs][1] and are related to the fact that we always [scroll to the top][2] after a short delay once a new doc is rendered. (So, it is a race condition.)

2. `stale element reference: element is not attached to the page document`
    I've seen this occur in tests that [use the `getLink()` helper][3]. It might be related to the fact that the links can appear in two places, either in the topbar (if the window is wide enough) or in the sidenav. This changes dynamically depending on the window's width.

3. `javascript error: document unloaded while waiting for result`
    This happens mostly in the [API pages specs][4] (in any of them), but I've seen it in other specs too (with much lower frequency though). I have no idea what might be causing this.

##
Other things we (don't) know:

- We don't know exactly what triggered the flakes. Changes that happened around the same time the flakes started to appear and may have affected e2e tests (but without being clear how or why):
    - Upgrade to Chrome 62 (in 820bb7bd8).
    - Fix another flake related to Google Analytics (in 441e01c56).
- There is a PR that might address (or at least considerably reduce) the first two flakes: #20117
- I don't think we have been able to reproduce the 3rd one locally (I haven't).
- As pointed out by @petebacondarwin, it seems as if protractor is not properly waiting for Angular. Could be an issue with (a) Protractor, (b) ChromeDriver, (c) Zones, (d) the Testability service, (e) all of the above. 
- There is an ongoing investigation :smiley:

##
Considering this is a major pain point for all PRs atm, @petebacondarwin has suggested (and I agree) that we should move the e2e tests into a selarate optional job, while we investigate.

[1]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/dcf88408314ccc384d827715c29d25f3a12c8d00/aio/e2e/app.e2e-spec.ts#L42-L60
[2]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/dcf88408314ccc384d827715c29d25f3a12c8d00/aio/src/app/app.component.ts#L215-L216
[3]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/dcf88408314ccc384d827715c29d25f3a12c8d00/aio/e2e/app.e2e-spec.ts#L14
[4]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/dcf88408314ccc384d827715c29d25f3a12c8d00/aio/e2e/api.e2e-spec.ts

@gkalpak move the e2e tests to an optional job sounds good if we don't have any potential fix in sight. 

@vikerman have you seen any issues related to e2e test flakes with Chrome 62 and protractor?

The AIO e2e tests are failing randomly.
This PR moves those tests to an optional Travis job while we investigate.
See https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/20159#issuecomment-341832801

body:
Some more info/findings:

- I reverted 441e01c56 and still get flakes, so that's not it.
- Still get flakes with Chrome 64 (dev).
- Most (all) `stale element reference` errors appear (if my understanding is correct) when trying to perform an action (e.g. `getText()`, `click()`, etc) on an element that has just been located by an element locator (e.g. `element(by.css('...')).getText()`). This is weird, because there is nothing that should have caused the element to be removed from the DOM.

##
From a quick look at the ChromeDriver source code:

- The `document unloaded while waiting for result` would be caused by a specific property missing from the `document` (as seen [here][1]).
- The `stale element reference` error, if the element was no longer reachable when calling [retrieveItem()][2], which could only happen (considering the element was previously reachable) if [clearStale()][3] has previosuly found the element to not be reachable. This check in turn depends on a [nodeRoot == document][4] check.

So, both of the above failures could be caused by the `document` reference changing unexpectedly.
For example, if a navigation happened at a point during the test when it should not.

[1]: https://cs.chromium.org/chromium/src/chrome/test/chromedriver/chrome/web_view_impl.cc?type=cs&q=%22$chrome_asyncScriptInfo%22&sq=package:chromium&l=758

[3]: https://cs.chromium.org/chromium/src/chrome/test/chromedriver/js/call_function.js?q=call_function.js&sq=package:chromium&dr&l=182
[4]: https://cs.chromium.org/chromium/src/chrome/test/chromedriver/js/call_function.js?q=call_function.js&sq=package:chromium&dr&l=197
